messages:
michael: Noticing a strange race when people import the AsyncClient at module scope and then run tests that use different event loops. Error: 'Task was destroyed but it is pending!' or 'RuntimeError: Event loop is closed'. Repro below.

anya: can you share minimal repro?

michael: simple script:
```py
# repro.py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()  # created at import-time
import asyncio
async def _call():
    await client.generate('x')
if __name__ == '__main__':
    asyncio.run(_call())
    asyncio.run(_call())
```
Run twice in same process or from pytest with subprocesses and uvloop sometimes flakes.

paul: sounds like background tasks (token refresh / keepalive) are created without binding to a running loop. If the client creates tasks on first await but was instantiated when no loop existed, the later loop may be closed before aclose runs.

anya: we should: 1) lazy-start background tasks on first await or __aenter__; 2) ensure aclose tolerates closing when loop already shut and logs actionable guidance; 3) provide sync-safe APIs for WSGI/threaded apps.

michael: Agreed. For immediate unblock I switched our tests to an async fixture that creates client within event loop:
```py
@pytest.fixture
async def client():
    async with AsyncClient() as c:
        yield c
```
That removed the flakiness.

paul: implementation note: prefer not to spawn tasks in __init__. Use an internal state machine: UNINITIALIZED -> INITIALIZING -> READY. On first async call do get_running_loop() and create tasks via loop.create_task. If you detect calls across different loop objects warn and raise in debug.

ci-bot: CI started for lazy-init branch build 1024

tess: small docs fix: add FAQ entry "Why am I seeing event loop closed errors?" and show patterns for sync, async, and pytest fixtures. Also mark the breaking behavioral change if we stop spawning tasks at import-time.

michael: opened issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/768 and will attach repro. planning to PR a lazy-init patch with tests that run subprocesses to emulate multiple run_until_complete cycles.

anya: follow-up: consider exporting a SyncClient wrapper that uses httpx.Client underneath so thread-based workloads don't accidentally cross event loops. add type stubs for both SyncClient and AsyncClient to avoid mypy confusion.

paul: one more: ensure __del__ does not try to close async resources on GC unless loop is running; prefer explicit aclose() and context-manager usage. Add a runtime warning if client is GC'd with open resources.

michael: thanks all, will push WIP PR and tag reviewers. closing thread after merge.
